title: Dual-time CFL iteration index
overview: idualtime is an optional integer selector read by Iteration::Init. Missing entries retain Iteration::dualtime = 0; value 1 selects innerSteps rather than outerSteps when evaluating the CFL ramp.
principle: The schedule index is outerSteps for physical-time indexing and innerSteps when idualtime == 1. This selector changes which iteration counter drives the CFL schedule; it does not itself define the physical-time integration method or a physical time increment.
architecture: Iteration::Init checks FindDataEntry("idualtime") before reading the integer value. TimeStep::CalcCfl passes the selected mode to CflIterationIndex. The combined schedule is parameter/cfl-ramp.

proves: The input is optional and defaults to zero when absent.
The value 1 selects innerSteps for the CFL schedule; non-dual mode uses outerSteps.
does_not_prove: That every solver supports dual-time stepping.
That idualtime selects a particular time_integral algorithm or guarantees a physical-time accuracy order.

verification.scope: Source-backed counter-selection policy; declaration does not imply test execution.

examples.title: Physical-time versus dual-time indexing
examples.calculation: With idualtime = 0, the schedule index is 10. With idualtime = 1, the schedule index is 40.
examples.result: The same CFL schedule can advance according to a different iteration counter.
examples.limitations: This does not define how currTime is advanced or prove that a selected solver path uses dual-time stepping.

formulas.title: CFL schedule index selection
formulas.plain: i = outerSteps when idualtime != 1; i = innerSteps when idualtime == 1
formulas.assumptions: This is the CflIterationIndex policy for the audited NS time-step path. Missing input defaults to zero during Iteration::Init.

caveats: This selector governs CFL schedule indexing, not the full dual-time algorithm.
Missing parameter defaults to physical-time indexing.
